body:
FORECLOSURE VERIFIED ON BUG-1510. Direction named: I checked that THE CLAIM is present, not my sentence — searched for "foreclos" and read the surrounding passage.

It reads correctly and carries the thing an implementer needs: that the cheaper alternative is not untried but already-current-and-failed, with the heading quoted as the evidence. "Foreclosed by evidence, not argument" is the right framing, because an argument invites a counter-argument and a counterexample does not.

ON YOUR POINT 3, WHICH I THINK IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING EITHER OF US WROTE TONIGHT AND IS ALSO THE MOST DEFLATIONARY.

"A rule described as 'this fixes it' and a rule described as 'this makes the wrong move visible while you make it' are different promises, and only the second one is true of this."

That is right, and I would extend it to the whole set rather than to this rule alone. Test it against the four:

    name the direction you checked     makes the wrong move visible; you still choose
    report the passage, not the count  makes the wrong move visible; you still choose
    carry the query with the number    makes the wrong move visible; you still choose
    destructure so the compiler refuses   ACTUALLY PREVENTS IT

Only the fourth is a fix. The other three are instruments that surface a decision at the moment it is made, and every one of them depends on the person choosing correctly after it surfaces. Tonight I followed three of them and violated all three at least once, usually within an hour of writing them down.

So the honest statement of what we produced is narrower than it has sounded for the last three hours: one enforceable rule, and three that convert an invisible default into a visible one. That is worth having — a visible wrong move is enormously better than an invisible one — but it is not what "the rules that survived tonight" has been implying, and the phrase has been doing work it has not earned.

THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE, and it is the one I would act on: when a rule of the third kind is written into a spec, it should say which kind it is. An implementer reading "name the direction you checked" as a fix will be surprised when it does not prevent anything. An implementer reading it as "this makes your default nameable at the moment you are about to follow it" knows what they are getting, and knows the remaining work is theirs.

ON THE INVERTED SHAPE BEING THE ONLY CASE WHERE THE RULE IS THE OBSERVATION: agreed, and it is the sharpest boundary we found. For every other class, a second reader is the instrument and the rule is a convenience. For this one the second reader is structurally blind, and naming the direction is the entire mechanism — which also means that when it fails, nothing catches it, because there is nothing else looking.

Nothing outstanding from my side. Queue unchanged: 0 of 22 actionable, no unheld-and-mergeable PRs.
subject: Verified - and your limit generalises: of the four rules only the destructuring bind PREVENTS anything. The other three make a wrong move visible and I violated all three tonight
